item.title: Capitulum 7 · Lūdus Plāgōsī (Flogger's school) · English → Latin, then Latin × 2
item.description: Vir Rōmānus, Part I, chapter 7 (132 AD, Porcellus is 11; level A2). It is the year 132. Porcellus is eleven, but he cannot read. Bucca sends him to school, to the teacher Plāgōsus, who has a long cane. At the same time Marcus becomes a philosopher and sleeps on the ground. Porcellus also sleeps on the ground. Always has. Grammar: Dēclīnātiō tertia: rēx, rēgis · adiectīva: bonus, bona, bonum · fortis, forte. Full cast; narrator Iulia (Rossana). Every line in English, then in Latin; then the whole chapter in Latin only, twice.

item.title: Capitulum 6 · Iter Brundisium (The road to Brundisium) · English → Latin, then Latin × 2
item.description: Vir Rōmānus, Part I, chapter 6 (131 AD, Porcellus is 10; level A2). It is the year 131. Bucca's cousin dies in Brundisium and leaves Bucca an inheritance. Bucca, Porcellus, Bibulus, Sabidius and Hannibal make a long trip along the Via Appia: bad water, boatmen, frogs, mosquitoes. What is the inheritance? Not money. Grammar: Ego, tū, nōs, vōs: persōna prīma et secunda · Rōmam, Rōmā, Brundisium. Full cast; narrator Iulia (Rossana). Every line in English, then in Latin; then the whole chapter in Latin only, twice.

item.title: Capitulum 5 · Vīlla et caper (The villa and the goat) · English → Latin, then Latin × 2
item.description: Vir Rōmānus, Part I, chapter 5 (130 AD, Porcellus is 9; level A2). It is the year 130. Porcellus eats too much, and Bucca is poor. So Porcellus goes to the senator Pinguis's villa, near the sea. There he will look after a goat. The goat is called Hannibal. Marcus is at the villa too, as a guest. Pliny's letter, a goat, a roof, a fish pond: everything will end badly. Grammar: Ubi? Unde? Quōcum? Ablātīvus cum praepositiōnibus · Rōmae, domī, rūrī. Full cast; narrator Iulia (Rossana). Every line in English, then in Latin; then the whole chapter in Latin only, twice.

item.title: Capitulum 4 · Servus inūtilis (The useless slave) · English → Latin, then Latin × 2
item.description: Vir Rōmānus, Part I, chapter 4 (128 AD, Porcellus is 7; level A2). It is the year 128. Bucca works too hard and wants to buy a slave. In the forum a trader sells her a Greek slave, a philosopher, called Sabidius. Sabidius talks a lot and does nothing. Then Bibulus is ill, and a strange doctor comes. Grammar: Cui? Datīvus · is, ea, id · numerī ad mīlle · pecūnia. Full cast; narrator Iulia (Rossana). Every line in English, then in Latin; then the whole chapter in Latin only, twice.

item.title: Capitulum 3 · Vērissimus et Falsissimus (Truest and Falsest) · English → Latin, then Latin × 2
item.description: Vir Rōmānus, Part I, chapter 3 (127 AD, Porcellus is 6; level A1–A2). It is the year 127. Porcellus is six and he is a naughty boy. Today the emperor Hadrian comes to the Caelian hill and gives Marcus a horse. Porcellus wants a horse too. But Porcellus does not have a horse. Porcellus has a pig. Grammar: Quem? Quid? Accūsātīvus · verba: -at, -et, -it · imperātīvus · vocātīvus. Full cast; narrator Iulia (Rossana). Every line in English, then in Latin; then the whole chapter in Latin only, twice.

item.title: Capitulum 2 · Garum Pompēiānum (The Pompeii fish sauce) · English → Latin, then Latin × 2
item.description: Vir Rōmānus, Part I, chapter 2 (125 AD, Porcellus is 4; level A1–A2). It is the year 125. Porcellus is four. Bucca has bad fish sauce and wants the best: Scaurus's fish sauce, from the town of Pompeii. But Bibulus knows something about Pompeii. Bucca, Porcellus and Bibulus make the trip. There they will find a clever man, and walls full of filthy words. Grammar: Cuius? Genitīvus · numerī I–X · quot?. Full cast; narrator Iulia (Rossana). Every line in English, then in Latin; then the whole chapter in Latin only, twice.

item.title: Capitulum 1 · Stēlla stulta (The stupid star) · English → Latin, then Latin × 2
item.description: Vir Rōmānus, Part I, chapter 1 (121 AD, Porcellus is 0; level A1–A2). In this chapter it is night in Rome. Three astrologers see a new star. The star leads them to the Caelian hill, where there are two houses: a big house and a dirty cookshop. The astrologers are looking for a king. Whom will they find? A pig? A baby? Both? Grammar: Quis? Nōminātīvus: ūnus et multī · est / sunt · -ne, num, quis, quid. Full cast; narrator Iulia (Rossana). Every line in English, then in Latin; then the whole chapter in Latin only, twice.
